content.title: What are Classes and Objects?
content.description: A class is a blueprint that defines the properties and behaviors of an object, while an object is a real instance of that class with its own data and functionality.

content.content: Java is an Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) language. Everything revolves around classes and objects. A class defines what an object should contain, and an object is the actual entity created using that class.

content.title: Why Learn Classes & Objects?
content.content: Classes and objects are the foundation of Object-Oriented Programming. Understanding them is essential before learning inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation, and abstraction.
Understanding a Class
A class is a user-defined blueprint that groups related variables (called fields) and methods (called behaviors) together. No memory is allocated for a class until an object is created.

content.title: Creating a Class
Class Components
content.description: A class typically contains fields (variables), constructors, methods, and nested classes if required.

content.content: Understanding an Object
An object is an instance of a class. When an object is created using the new keyword, memory is allocated, and the object's fields and methods become accessible.
Accessing Object Members
The dot (.) operator is used to access an object's variables and methods.

content.title: Accessing Fields and Methods

content.content: Multiple Objects
Multiple objects can be created from the same class. Each object maintains its own copy of instance variables while sharing the same method definitions.

content.title: Multiple Objects Example
Important Note
content.content: One class can create any number of objects, and each object stores its own independent data.
Instance Variables and Methods
Instance variables belong to individual objects, whereas instance methods operate on the data stored inside those objects.
Constructors Overview
A constructor is a special method that is automatically called when an object is created. It initializes the object's data.
Class vs Object
Memory Representation
Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Blueprint and House
content.content: A class is like the blueprint of a house that describes its structure. An object is the actual house built using that blueprint. Many houses can be constructed from the same blueprint, just as many objects can be created from one class.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Questions about classes, objects, object creation, constructors, instance variables, reference variables, and memory allocation are among the most common Java interview topics.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Can methods be called without creating an object?
items.answer: Instance methods require an object. Only static methods can be called without creating an object.

items.question: Why is the new keyword necessary?
items.answer: Because it allocates memory for the object and returns a reference to it.

items.question: What happens if object fields are not initialized?
items.answer: Java automatically assigns default values such as 0, false, or null depending on the data type.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: A class defines the structure, while objects represent real entities created from that structure. Multiple objects can be created from a single class.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: A class is a blueprint for creating objects.
Dot operator is used to access object members.
Each object has its own copy of instance variables.
